column1: # QE checks (G): what a Korean line must realise, given the Japanese clause features the rules decided (L: aux.tsv
# folding, links, negFn). A row flags a line; it never reroutes. Spec: spec/checks.md. Cases: check.cases.tsv.
# No learned input: the Japanese side is the IR clause, the Korean side the sentence facts of qe/ko.py.
#   scope   unit (the Korean sentence aligned with the clause's sentence, else the whole line) | last (the
#           sentence that closes the unit) | line (numbers and names of the whole line)
#   when    clause atoms joined by &: c.feat=v|w, c.feat!=v, c.flag, !c.flag; feats pol negFn force voice bene
#           polite link linkSub mod (modality list); flags rare (れる/られる in the clause), qmark (？ in its sentence),
#           final (no clause link: the clause ends its sentence)
#   unless  unit atoms joined by | (any one exempts): any.feat=v (some clause of the unit has it); - for none
#   ko      Korean atoms joined by | (any one satisfies the check): neg, pot_neg, pot (either potential), jana, oblig,
#           prohib, q, hon, calque, plain_neg (a negative that is not 잖 and not a question), neg1 (exactly one
#           negative), before (-기 전에); !atom = must not hold; line scope: numbers, names
# For one clause, among the rows of one spec id that match, the most specific (most when atoms) decides: an
# exception is a row of the same spec with more atoms.

column10: a negated clause needs a negative in its sentence (안, 않다, 못, 없다, 아니다, 모르다), a potential negative, -잖아 or an obligation
ないうちに (before it cools) is -기 전에 as well as -지 않을 때
a potential negative (行けない, 読めない) needs -ㄹ 수 없다 or 못
a prohibition (するな, ちゃだめ, てはいけない) needs -지 마, -면 안 되다
same, decided as the clause's force
なくてもいい is "need not" (-지 않아도 되다), not a prohibition: it needs the negative only
なければならない, なきゃ need -어야 하다/되다
same, decided as the clause's modality
a rhetorical じゃない(か) is a confirmation: a plain negative statement flips it
a double negation (ないわけではない) is positive: one plain negative flips it
archaic volitional ん (行かん) is "let's", not a negation
a question that ends its sentence with ？ is asked in Korean too
an imperative is not "can": no -ㄹ 수 있다/없다 unless the Japanese has a potential
an honorific predicate (いらっしゃる, お〜になる) needs -시- or an honorific verb
てもらう is not -어 받다 (a calque)
every number of the source appears in the Korean (digits, Sino-Korean or native numerals)
every person or place name the analyzer reads appears, transliterated
